messages.content: "A car starts from rest and travels a distance of 120 meters in 10 seconds. What is the speed of the car at the end of this time period? After reaching this speed, the car continues to accelerate for another 5 seconds from 12 m/s until it reaches a final speed doubling the initial speed. The final speed is twice the speed calculated in the first part. What is the acceleration of the car in this second phase?"

Second part: car continues to accelerate for another 5 seconds from 12 m/s until it reaches a final speed doubling the initial speed. But then final speed doubling the initial speed would be 24 m/s. That matches the first part speed. So maybe the second phase starts at 12 m/s and ends at 24 m/s after 5s. That would be acceleration a = (v - u)/t = (24-12)/5 = 12/5 = 2.4 m/s^2. So same acceleration. But the phrasing "doubling the initial speed" refers to initial speed of second phase? That would be 12 m/s, final 24 m/s. So acceleration 2.4 m/s^2.
